note: Classification of the 568 findings of apps/lab/audit/content/findings.json by this lane, 2026-10-07. A finding is in the list when it describes a way to get around a review rule, to read or change data without the right, to lock or break the service for other persons, or a weakness of sign-in, tokens, webhooks, or the CI trust. The other findings are not in the list.

classes.review-bypass: A way around a review rule.
classes.data-access: A read or a change of data without the right.
classes.denial: The service stops, slows, or costs more for other persons.
classes.trust: A weakness of sign-in, tokens, webhooks, or the CI trust.

handling.hold-path: A public issue must not give the step path, the chain, or the cost numbers before the fix is in production.
handling.normal: A public issue with the full detail adds little for an attacker.

findings.title: All Better Auth routes are served, and a session of any account that can sign in is sufficient for them
findings.actor: A script in the page of a signed-in maintainer, or a person with a copy of D1 while a copied session is live.
findings.needsFirst: A session of one of the 5 accounts with push permission. The record found no script injection, and the page has a CSP with a nonce.
findings.checkedByThisLane: apps/web/src/server.ts:82-87 sends each /api/auth/ path to the library with no path filter. packages/security/src/auth.ts:21-79 has no disabledPaths.
findings.difficulty: high from outside (a second failure must come first), low with a session
findings.publicIssueAdds: The name of the route that returns the GitHub user token, and the fact that the sign-in App is the App that writes the required check. A reader of the code can find the route list in the documentation of the sign-in library.
findings.judgment: The most useful path of the record for an attacker with a foothold. It gives a token that can, by the GitHub documentation, set the required Visonaut check. It cannot push, approve, or merge (record, not tested by this lane).

findings.title: The signed session token reaches page scripts, and the raw database token works as a credential
findings.actor: A person who can read the production D1 database, or a script in the page of a signed-in maintainer.
findings.needsFirst: Read access to D1 (the Cloudflare account, an export, or a backup), or a script injection.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/auth.ts:53 loads the bearer plugin with no option. apps/web/src/api/index.ts:220-222 copies each session header to the answer.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The statement that one session row of D1 is a complete credential. This raises the value of each copy, export, and backup of D1.
findings.judgment: Same group and same fix list as TRUST-01. One issue covers both.

findings.title: GitHub OAuth user tokens are stored and never read
findings.actor: The same as TRUST-01.
findings.needsFirst: A session of an account that signed in.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/auth.ts:36-38 stores the tokens encrypted and updates them at each sign-in. The route that returns them is in the library, not in the repository.
findings.difficulty: high from outside, low with a session
findings.publicIssueAdds: That the stored tokens are readable through a route, and that they are tokens of a GitHub App with repository permissions.
findings.judgment: The fix removes the tokens: a hook stores none, and one UPDATE in production clears the rows of today. You authorized that UPDATE on 2026-10-07.

findings.title: Anonymous requests cost D1 work before the 401
findings.actor: Each caller on the internet.
findings.checkedByThisLane: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:123-126 reads the project and :130 builds the sign-in library before the credential check at :194.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The cost of one request with no credential (2 to 3 round trips and 76 to 77 D1 statements, by the record) and the route that costs most. The time is also measurable from outside with no credential.
findings.judgment: The only group with an actor that needs nothing first. The effect is cost and a slow service, not data. The first fix of the speed list (no schema check on a request) removes most of it.

findings.title: Ingest routes do database work, and one outbound request, before they check the credential
findings.actor: Each caller on the internet.
findings.checkedByThisLane: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:163-172 decodes the shard key before a capability check. The reads before the token check (workflow-owned.ts:1177-1209) are from the record: this lane did not open that file.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Which ingest route does database work and one outbound request before the credential check, and that 401 or 404 tells if a run number exists.
findings.judgment: Same group as AUTH-07. Low effect each, but no prerequisite.

findings.title: Rate limiting covers only the auth routes, uses D1, and takes the client address from X-Forwarded-For
findings.actor: Each caller on the internet.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/auth.ts:52 turns the limiter on with D1 storage and sets no client address header.
findings.publicIssueAdds: That each request to an auth route writes a limiter row to D1 with no credential (a D1 write that repeats with traffic, your standing rule 1), that callers with zero or several X-Forwarded-For values share one bucket, and that the private API has no application limit.
findings.judgment: Not a way around the limit (record). It is a way to cause D1 writes with no credential.

findings.title: A signed-in account without repository access causes 2 GitHub App requests on each private request
findings.actor: An organization member without push permission (about 5 accounts), or a person who lost access and kept a session.
findings.needsFirst: A sign-in. Only members of the organization can sign in (record: the App is private).
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/github.ts:226-228 throws not_maintainer after the GitHub requests, and :251-256 makes 2 requests for an unknown login. No negative cache: record.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The method to use up the request budget of the App that writes the required check. With OPS-01, a failed read then locks a check until a manual repair.
findings.judgment: The actor is one of a few known accounts and gains nothing. The effect reaches each pull request of ariakit/ariakit, so the path stays out of a public issue until the fix is live.

findings.title: A Reject of a carried approval is dropped at the next push
findings.actor: An account with push permission that pushes again or starts the workflow again.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/service/src/local-comparison.ts:21-37: the reuse rule tests approved and not revoked, and has no test for a later Reject.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little. The actor may approve the own pull request by the earlier decision D09 (record). The gain is that no new decision row names the actor.
findings.judgment: A defect of the review record between 5 trusted accounts. A normal public bug report.

findings.title: A check that is locked after "success" keeps "success" after Reject or Undo
findings.actor: No person starts it directly. It needs a failed GitHub read at the time of a Reject.
findings.needsFirst: A failed read of the check, then a Reject or an Undo on the same commit.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little alone. With the path of TRUST-02 a failed read can be caused, so the two issues must not link the paths before the fixes are live.
findings.judgment: Rows 1 to 3 of the fix list of D-OPS-01 are first in the plan for this reason.

findings.title: Pull request code selects the comparison settings, and the loosest settings make each change unchanged
findings.actor: The author of a pull request with push permission.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:46-63 accepts a threshold from 0 to 1 and each maxDiffPixels value. No service limit: record.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little. The contract already records that capture code can supply false pixels (record: decision A02).
findings.judgment: No new right. The run header will show the count of looser captures.

findings.title: On main, new and removed identities reach the baseline with no human decision and no upper bound
findings.actor: Merged code, or a wrong test selection on main.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing: the behavior is a rule of the contract.
findings.judgment: A reliability risk, not an attack path.

findings.title: "Equivalent merge check retired" makes the newest Visonaut check neutral also when the tested result failed
findings.actor: No person starts it directly. It needs a check row with no binding (old data or a stopped begin request).
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little. The effect on GitHub is not verified.
findings.judgment: Low and not verified.

findings.title: The readiness gate accepts a truncated image in all engines
findings.actor: No actor: a cut connection in Firefox, or a short stored object.
findings.needsFirst: Firefox, which is outside the browser scope of D-RES-04.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: A reviewer can approve a part image. Not a path for another person.

findings.title: No request reaches POST /validate, but the contract says the Worker validates uploads
findings.actor: The holder of an ingest capability: the Submit job. After D-OPS-04, a pull request of an account with push permission can replace that job.
findings.checkedByThisLane: record (apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:1066; a repository test asserts that the comparator is not called)
findings.publicIssueAdds: That the service stores upload bytes after a size and SHA-256 check only, and serves them from a public URL of visonaut.com. The image route sends nosniff and a sandbox CSP (record).
findings.judgment: This is item 1 of the list What still needs your word. Another lane of this round has that question.

findings.title: The QUARANTINE bucket no longer holds images; facts and options for the two-bucket rule (S01, D16)
findings.actor: The same as CMP-01.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The same as CMP-01.
findings.judgment: Same fact as CMP-01, seen from storage.

findings.title: The executor digest D is a declared text, not a measured hash; nothing checks which adapter ran
findings.actor: A person with push permission to a branch of ariakit/ariakit.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing: the capture job already runs the code of the pull request.
findings.judgment: D-OPS-04 removes the value. The kind security is strong for it (record).

findings.title: The Submit job installs the CLI by version only, the saved consumer patch shows a digest check that is not live, and the pinned blobs use action tags
findings.actor: A person who can publish the npm package visonaut, or who controls an action tag.
findings.needsFirst: The npm account or the action repository.
findings.checkedByThisLane: record (the live app.yml of ariakit/ariakit installs the CLI by version)
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing that the public workflow file does not show.
findings.judgment: A normal supply-chain statement.

findings.title: The ingest capability renews itself without OIDC, also after Submit
findings.actor: A person who gets a capability out of a Submit job.
findings.needsFirst: A failure of the Submit job that shows the capability.
findings.checkedByThisLane: apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:444-448 returns a new capability with a new 600 second life in each answer.
findings.publicIssueAdds: That the capability can be renewed with no new OIDC token. The gain is baseline data of a public project.
findings.judgment: Low gain, and it needs a leak first.

findings.title: An OIDC token is accepted again inside its 10 minutes, and one audience serves three endpoints
findings.actor: A person who gets an OIDC token of a CI job inside its life (5 to 10 minutes).
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/oidc.ts:129-130 requires jti and has a 10 minute maximum age. Nothing stores jti: record.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little.
findings.judgment: Low. The fix is not in a settled list: check that the issue plan has it or drops it.

findings.title: A signed webhook body is accepted again under a new delivery ID
findings.actor: A person who has a signed webhook body.
findings.needsFirst: A captured body. The record found no way for an outside person to get one.
findings.checkedByThisLane: packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:27-29 reads the delivery ID from a header, and :55 signs only the body.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little. The effect is a second sign-out of one user.
findings.judgment: Low.

findings.title: There is no procedure to rotate a secret outside database recovery
findings.actor: No actor: a gap in the operations guide.
findings.publicIssueAdds: That no rotation procedure exists.
findings.judgment: Low. A documentation task.

findings.title: For mutations, the origin check runs after the session and GitHub checks
findings.actor: A client that sends a valid cookie and a foreign Origin header.
findings.checkedByThisLane: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:194-208: the maintainer check runs before requireSameOrigin.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little.
findings.judgment: Cost only.

findings.title: The origin rule differs for each route, and production also answers on workers.dev
findings.actor: Each caller of the workers.dev host.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The second host name. It is in the public Wrangler file and in the public deploy logs.
findings.judgment: The API answers 403 on that host (record).

findings.title: Production also answers on visonaut.ariakit.workers.dev
findings.actor: The same as AUTH-10.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The same as AUTH-10.
findings.judgment: Same fact as AUTH-10.

findings.title: Duplicate and unused identity routes, and document drift
findings.actor: No actor: routes with no caller.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Unused surface.

findings.title: The access level comes from the HTTP method and a copied pattern
findings.actor: No actor today: no route has a wrong level.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: A design note.

findings.title: Small gaps in the response headers
findings.actor: No actor: missing response headers.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing: each header is visible in each answer.
findings.judgment: Defense in depth.

findings.title: The production comparator binds D1, R2, and the operations queue, but its code uses none of them
findings.actor: No actor today: the Worker has no route and no caller.
findings.needsFirst: A code change of the comparison Worker.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: More access than the code needs. Not reachable.

findings.title: The production validator Worker has D1, R2, and queue bindings that its code does not use
findings.actor: The same as CMP-02.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Same fact as CMP-02.

findings.title: After a sign-out in another tab, an open run page keeps its content and all its controls
findings.actor: A person at the same browser profile after a sign-out in another tab.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: The person sees what was on screen. No request works (record).

findings.title: The auth rate limit answers 429 after three sign-in starts in 10 seconds; the page says "could not start, try again" and enables the button at once
findings.actor: A caller that starts sign-in 3 times in 10 seconds in a shared limiter bucket.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Little. It is the user side of AUTH-14.
findings.judgment: A text defect. Keep the limiter numbers out of the issue of AUTH-14.

findings.title: A failed GitHub read marks a check "ambiguous" forever
findings.actor: No person starts it directly: one failed GitHub read locks a check.
findings.needsFirst: A failed read (a 5xx, a rate limit answer, or a time-out).
findings.publicIssueAdds: That a locked check needs a manual D1 repair. See TRUST-02 for the one path that can cause failed reads.
findings.judgment: A reliability defect. First in the plan.

findings.title: An ambiguous check with a newer status starts an endless status loop, and each cron tick adds one more loop
findings.actor: No actor: it follows OPS-01.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing more than OPS-01.
findings.judgment: Cost that grows with each cron tick.

findings.title: The real run inventory uses 72.9% of its 16 MiB write limit; at about 5,260 captures each Submit fails
findings.actor: A pull request that adds captures (1.38 times the count of today), or normal growth of the suite.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The capture count at which each Submit fails, and that a stuck run holds 1 of the 5 run slots for 24 to 30 hours (record).
findings.judgment: It happened by accident on 2026-10-04 (record). The actor is a trusted account.

findings.title: A run with more than about 5,270 captures cannot be stored (1.38 times today), and the limits do not agree
findings.actor: The same as STORE-01.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The same as STORE-01.
findings.judgment: Same limit as STORE-01.

findings.title: A capacity pause refused Submit after the complete capture: 5 failed Submit steps in one afternoon, and two main commits keep a red check
findings.actor: No actor: the capacity stop.
findings.needsFirst: 5 active runs, or a database above 2 GiB.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The two numbers of the stop. They are in the public code.
findings.judgment: A reliability defect with a real incident.

findings.title: Many tables only grow, and admission stops new runs at 2 GiB
findings.actor: No actor: tables that only grow.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Growth, not an attack.

findings.title: Operational tables only grow; the capacity stop is the only brake
findings.actor: No actor.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Same family as D1-10.

findings.title: Three model reads at the same time need 105 to 109 MB of live JavaScript heap at today's size; the isolate limit is 128 MB
findings.actor: A signed-in maintainer who reviews fast.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Memory of one isolate. Maintainers only.

findings.title: A delivery that cannot be processed is retried every 5 minutes without a limit, and the reason is not logged
findings.actor: No actor: a webhook delivery that cannot be processed.
findings.needsFirst: A pull request with no merge commit.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: A retry with no limit: cost and one open alert.

findings.title: 25 candidates that cannot be deleted stop all later image deletions
findings.actor: No actor: it needs a manual data change.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Image deletion stops. No data is lost.

findings.title: One command can have about 6,000 targets, and each target adds 4 statements and 2.4 KB to one batch
findings.actor: A signed-in maintainer who sends one command with thousands of targets.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Maintainers only.

findings.title: Wide rows and API bounds that can meet D1 limits
findings.actor: The same as STATE-09.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Same bound as STATE-09.

findings.title: A decision fails with 409 when any other write of the project commits at the same time
findings.actor: Two writers of one project at the same instant.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: A lost decision that the reviewer sees and repeats.

findings.title: Scripts: `pnpm check` is not the CI gate, two package scripts bypass the guarded deploy path, and the public adapter pins one Node patch version
findings.actor: A person with the Cloudflare credential on a laptop.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: Two scripts go around the guarded deploy path. Only the owner of the credential can run them.

findings.title: The environment model (top level is preview, env.production is production) has specific risks
findings.actor: The same as HYG-19.
findings.publicIssueAdds: Nothing.
findings.judgment: A risk of a wrong deploy by the owner.

findings.title: A stopped scheduler, a dead-lettered message, or a killed pass raises no signal
findings.actor: No actor.
findings.needsFirst: A stopped scheduler or a dead message.
findings.publicIssueAdds: That no signal comes from outside the service when the scheduler stops.
findings.judgment: A monitoring gap.

findings.title: Logs and traces use defaults only; there is no export and no alert from outside the service
findings.actor: No actor.
findings.publicIssueAdds: The same as OPS-09.
findings.judgment: A monitoring gap.
